reasoning: Noun plus adjective, not a construct, so تجربة keeps its taa marbuta e. The adjective ends in the Palestinian -iyye.

عين has long ee, written kasra plus ya. The usual Ramallah form is تكرم عينك tikram 3eenik, where the verb agrees with 'eye' and only the suffix marks the addressee; تكرمي treats the verb as agreeing with the woman.

romanization: laa 7awla wa laa quwwata illa billaah
vowelled_arabic: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰه
reasoning: A fixed religious formula said daily in Ramallah with its classical shape and case vowels intact, so ق keeps [q] and the fatha endings are pronounced.
ق in لاقى is a glottal stop. The 2fs of a final-weak verb is identical to the 2ms here; شغل takes an epenthetic u: shughul.
b-imperfect first person with long uu, and -ik for the female addressee.
Palestinian passive with the it- prefix; انخرب inkharab is an equally common variant.
Form II with shadda on the و. The optative drops the b- prefix, as blessings always do.
Form X; ق glottalises in ordinary news-and-work talk. Initial hamza on the alif seat is not romanized.
Form X geminate verb, doubled l from the shadda.
عجل is the Palestinian word for a wheel or tyre and ع is a moon letter, so the article stays il-. فقع 'burst' has a glottal ق.
The first short vowel drops and ذ is a plain d in Palestinian speech, so it is respelled د. More careful speakers say nabiiz.
mish negates the participle, as Palestinian requires. The feminine participle faayte plus the dative -li gives faaytitli; the exact vowel of that linking syllable varies between speakers.
Urban Palestinian has no interdental ظ; it falls together with ض, so this is said aDunn. Many speakers prefer the fully colloquial على ما بظن.
MSA ظلّ is spelled and said with ض in Palestinian. Geminate final l; also used as 'kept on doing'.
Form V participle with the Palestinian mi- prefix and shadda on the و. The th here is t plus h across a syllable boundary, not the ث sound.
Kasra on the ب distinguishes it from baraka 'blessing'. Taa marbuta after ك is e.

meaning_fix: veterinary (adjective); a vet is دكتور بيطري duktoor beeTari
reasoning: MSA ay becomes long ee in Palestinian, so beeTari, with emphatic T. On its own the word is an adjective, not the noun 'veterinarian'.
همس is a literary verb; in Ramallah conversation whispering is washwash or حكى بصوت واطي. The romanization itself is straightforward.
Long oo in moosam; ز is a sun letter, so the article assimilates. زيتون has long ee.
Everyday word for a road accident. Urban Ramallah speakers without an interdental usually say 7aades, which is the uncertain part of the transcription.
ي is a moon letter but ص is a sun letter, so il-yoom but iS-Sub7. Long oo in yoom.
bi plus the article gives bil- before the moon letter ع, and the final ق is a glottal stop.
3indi is negated with ما, which marks it as Palestinian usage. سخونية has long uu and the -iyye ending; it is the everyday word for fever, not حرارة.
Plural participle plus the 2ms suffix; ق is a glottal stop, giving mishtaa'iinak.
The headword is missing its alif: the word is عامية 3aammiyye with long aa and a doubled م. Written عمية it would read 3amiyye 'blindness', so the spelling should be corrected.
